brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.evidence: Four full hex bases at (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0), (2,0) with four drained bins in them.

requirements.requirement: Water pipe running through the bases
requirements.evidence: run-1 starts at (-1,0) and passes through (0,0), (1,0), (2,0) on level 0; set to potable mode.
The pipe passes through all four cells, but the configurator does not model water flow or whether the pipe has an actual outlet into each bin; I did not add fittings or ports into the bins.

requirements.requirement: Materials suitable for water/soil (waterproofing, food/potable safety, UV/heat)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit only; material properties were not assessed.

finish.summary: Built a four-cell planter: four full hex bases in a straight row (q -1..2, r 0), each holding a third-depth drained bin filled with soil and planted with cabbage seedlings. A pipe run (run-1, set to potable mode) enters at the west end and passes straight through all four cells, so it feeds every cell. Open faces are capped and joints bolted; check_build is clear with meshClash clear. Caveats: the configurator checks fit only, so I have not verified water-tightness, pipe fittings for a real supply, or the suitability of the printed material for wet soil or potable water.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 1 run POTABLE: drinking water. No flexible hose anywhere: flexible PVC is NSF-50 (pool and spa) and is not rated for drinking water. Every fitting and length must be NSF-61 pressure pipe.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
